correctness.rationale: The small intersecting-family lemma forces the unique 4-member star colour class, with two complementary 3-member star/triangle classes; this bijects all colourings with 20 ordered pairs and 6 palette assignments. Induced bichromatic subgraphs are 3 disjoint edges, a 6-cycle plus isolated vertex, and a connected 7-vertex tree, respectively, establishing all quotient adjacencies and labelled degree 6. The once-subdivided K5 line-graph identification and quotient diameter 3 are proved analytically. The actual embedded verify.py path was executed successfully: two independent generators agree on exactly 120 colorings; two independent component algorithms agree on every move; full all-source BFS yields labelled shells (1,6,25,61,27) and quotient shells (1,4,6,9). No infinite inference is made from finite computations.

value.rationale: This classifies the complete Kempe adjacency geometry for optimal vertex colourings of the canonical Petersen graph, rather than counting a contrived filtered subset. The explicit line-graph identification reveals an unexpected structural quotient in natural directed-edge coordinates, while sharp radii, diameters, and uniform distance shells quantify minimum Kempe moves beyond the previously known connectivity theorem. It provides a reproducible finite benchmark; no universal or paper-sized extension is claimed.
